product.name: DJI compact wireless microphone kit in charging case (looks like the DJI Mic 3 / Mic Mini family; exact model not legibl
product.summary: Clamshell charging case in dark grey moulded plastic holding two clip-on wireless microphone transmitters (with furry windscreens fitted) and one receiver in a docking tray, with four white charge LEDs on the front. The case is assumed to hold a single Li-ion pouch cell charged over USB-C and to feed the docked units through spring contacts; none of the internals are visible. Scale is taken from the hand and the roughly 28 mm transmitter body, so all dimensions are estimates and the model is drawn with the lid closed.
product.powerInput: USB-C, 5 V up to about 1.5 A (assumed; port not visible in the photo)

parts.name: Case base shell
parts.function: Lower housing half that carries the case electronics, the battery and the docking tray.
parts.evidence: Dark grey matte base held in the hand, with four LED windows on the front face.
parts.unknowns: Wall thickness and how the tray is retained; inspect under the tray or the feet for screws.

parts.name: Case lid shell
parts.function: Hinged upper half that covers the docked units and stores accessories.
parts.evidence: Open grey lid at the rear with a black inner liner.

parts.name: Lid hinge pin
parts.function: Pivots the lid on the base along the rear edge.
parts.evidence: The lid stays attached and opens about the rear edge; the pin itself is not visible.
parts.unknowns: May have a friction or spring detent; check from the rear.

parts.name: Docking tray insert
parts.function: Black inner moulding with pockets that locate the two transmitters and the receiver over their charging contacts.
parts.evidence: Black glossy insert with shaped pockets; the empty right-hand pocket is visible.
parts.unknowns: Real pocket depth and shape; modelled as a flat plate.

parts.name: Tray screws
parts.function: Hold the docking tray to bosses in the base shell.
parts.evidence: Typical for charging cases; no screws visible, so the tray may be clipped or glued instead.
parts.unknowns: Existence and location; look under the pockets or labels.

parts.name: Wireless microphone transmitter (TX)
parts.function: Clip-on microphone that digitises audio and sends it by radio to the receiver; contains its own small cell, microphone and radio SoC.
parts.evidence: One light-grey cube with DJI logo held in the right hand, a second docked at the left under its windscreen.
parts.unknowns: Internals not visible: cell capacity, radio SoC, microphone type. Needs opening the transmitter.

parts.name: Furry windscreen
parts.function: Synthetic fur cover that reduces wind noise at the microphone port.
parts.material: synthetic fur over foam with a plastic twist-lock base
parts.evidence: Grey-white fur balls on top of both transmitters.
parts.unknowns: Shown compressed to fit the closed lid; free height is larger.

parts.name: Wireless receiver (RX)
parts.function: Receives audio from both transmitters and outputs it to a camera or phone.
parts.evidence: Black block docked in the centre of the tray with a small green indicator beside it.
parts.unknowns: Display, controls and outputs are not visible in this photo.

parts.name: Lid accessory liner
parts.function: Black insert in the lid with recesses that store small accessories.
parts.evidence: Black inner panel in the lid holding a round DJI-branded part.

parts.name: Clip magnets stored in lid
parts.function: Magnetic discs that hold a transmitter to clothing from behind the fabric.
parts.evidence: Round DJI-logo parts sitting in the lid recess; identity as clip magnets is inferred from the product type.
parts.unknowns: Could be one part with a ring around it; a close-up of the lid would settle it.

parts.name: Gold posts in lid
parts.function: Gold-coloured pins in the lid, possibly contacts or locating posts for a stored adapter.
parts.evidence: Two small gold pins visible at the left and right of the lid interior.
parts.unknowns: Purpose not clear; check whether they are wired or only mechanical.

parts.name: Latch magnet (base)
parts.function: Holds the lid closed against its partner in the lid.
parts.evidence: A rectangular latch feature is visible at the front lip; a magnet closure is typical.
parts.unknowns: May be a mechanical snap latch instead.

parts.name: Latch magnet (lid)
parts.function: Lid-side closure magnet that also triggers the lid sensor.
parts.evidence: Typical for this type of case.

parts.name: Case main PCB
parts.function: Carries the charger, the boost converter, the controller, the LEDs and the charging contacts.
parts.evidence: The LEDs and charging function require a board; it is not visible.
parts.unknowns: Real outline and whether it is one board or a board plus flex.

parts.name: Case Li-ion pouch cell
parts.function: Stores energy to recharge the transmitters and the receiver away from mains.
parts.evidence: A charging case with a charge gauge implies an internal cell.
parts.unknowns: Capacity and size; read the cell label or the rating print on the case.

parts.name: USB-C receptacle
parts.function: Power input for charging the case.
parts.evidence: Not visible; standard for this product class, probably on the rear or side.
parts.unknowns: Location, and whether it carries data.

parts.name: Battery charger IC
parts.function: Charges the case cell from USB with CC/CV control.
candidates: switching 1S charger family, for example TI BQ2589x or SGMicro equivalents
parts.evidence: Required for an internal Li-ion cell.

parts.name: Power inductor
parts.function: Energy storage for the switching charger or boost stage.
parts.evidence: Typical for a switching charger.

parts.name: 5 V boost / output switch
parts.function: Raises the cell voltage to about 5 V and switches it to the dock contacts.
parts.evidence: Docked units need a charge voltage above the cell voltage.
parts.unknowns: May be integrated in the charger IC.

parts.name: Case microcontroller
parts.function: Monitors the cell, drives the four LEDs, detects the lid and the docked units.
parts.evidence: A four-level gauge and dock detection need a small controller.

parts.name: Cell protection IC and MOSFET
parts.function: Disconnects the cell on over-charge, over-discharge or short circuit.
candidates: DW01 class with 8205 class dual MOSFET
parts.evidence: Standard for Li-ion packs; may sit on the cell's own small board.

parts.name: Lid hall sensor
parts.function: Senses the lid magnet so the case can wake, show the gauge and power the docked units.
parts.evidence: The LEDs are lit with the lid open, consistent with lid detection.

parts.name: Charge level LEDs
parts.function: Show the case battery level in four steps through the front wall.
parts.evidence: Four small white dots lit on the front of the base.
parts.unknowns: The LED windows sit higher on the wall than this board level, so light pipes or a separate small board are likely.

parts.name: Dock charging contacts
parts.function: Spring contacts that pass charge power and detection to each docked unit through the tray.
parts.evidence: The units charge when docked and no plug is used; the contacts are hidden under the docked parts.
parts.unknowns: Pin count and position; inspect the empty right-hand pocket. Real pin tips protrude through the tray.

parts.name: Resistors and capacitors
parts.function: Decoupling, feedback dividers, LED current limiting and USB-C CC pull-downs.
parts.evidence: Needed by the ICs above.

LED drive

connections.evidence: This is a wireless microphone set; the band is typical for this class.

controls.label: Open lid
controls.action: Opening the lid wakes the case and lights the four LEDs to show the battery level.

unknowns: Exact model (the DJI logo is visible, the model name is not); read the print on the case underside.
Everything inside the case is assumed: board outline, ICs, cell capacity and USB-C location. Open the case to confirm.
The transmitter and receiver internals (cells, radio SoC, microphones, display) are not visible and are modelled as single blocks.
Purpose of the two gold pins in the lid.
Whether the lid is held by magnets or a mechanical latch, and how the tray is fixed.
Buttons on the transmitters and the receiver are not visible, so they are not listed as controls.
verifySteps: Photograph the underside and rear of the case for the rating print (model, cell capacity, input) and the USB-C port position.
Photograph the empty dock pockets close up to count the charging contacts.
Measure the case and one transmitter with callipers to correct the scale.
Remove the tray and photograph the board on both sides to read the IC markings.
Measure the voltage on the dock contacts with the lid open and with it closed.
Photograph the lid interior close up to identify the stored accessories and the gold pins.
safety: The case and each unit contain lithium cells: do not puncture, bend or short them when opening, and pry away from the cell.
The clip magnets are strong: keep them away from pacemakers and magnetic cards, and out of reach of children.
Disconnect USB before opening the case; the dock contacts may be live from the internal cell.
